summary: Three InP surface preparations before Nb sputtering are compared: untreated, in-situ Ar+ milling, and sulfur passivation. S-passivation gives the cleanest, sharpest buried interface and higher $T_c$, yet single-photon $Q_i$ is similar for all three (about 84k-130k), indicating the resonators are not limited by loss at the Nb-InP interface.
motivation: How substrate oxide removal affects microwave loss in hybrid superconductor-semiconductor quantum devices is poorly understood.
method: Materials characterization of the metal-substrate interface (oxygen content, roughness, film damage, $T_c$) is combined with low-power microwave measurements of Nb resonators.
result: Single-photon $Q_i$ is roughly 130k (control), 97k (S-passivated) and 84k (Ar+ milled), so the cleaner interface does not translate into lower loss.
